transcript.text:
Hi everyone. I need to make a decision on the production rollout plan for the authentication-library patch. As a reminder, the patch addresses a critical vulnerability and has passed our security team's lab tests. The current draft proposes a Thursday 02:00 UTC canary for 60 minutes, followed by broad deployment on Friday.

Before I can approve any plan, our release policy requires a final round-robin check with application platform, reliability, and compliance. I need to hear from each of those areas and record any required rollout changes before approval. Can the representatives from application platform, reliability, and compliance each share their review and any changes they need incorporated into the plan?

transcript.text: While debugging an unrelated authentication test this morning, I confirmed that the Ledger service uses a custom fork of the library. Ledger must have the compatibility flag enabled before broad deployment, and it must be excluded from the canary until that flag is enabled. I have not updated the rollout document because the compatibility test completed only minutes ago.

transcript.text: I need to flag a reliability blocker. While preparing another maintenance window, I checked the current on-call rota and confirmed that I am the only engineer qualified to perform rollback for this patch during Wednesday 18:00–22:00 UTC. The Thursday 02:00 UTC slot has no qualified rollback engineer on the rota. Therefore the Thursday 02:00 UTC canary cannot be approved as proposed. To have confirmed rollback coverage, the canary must move to Wednesday 18:00 UTC. I haven't posted the staffing confirmation yet because the rota change is still being recorded, but the rota itself is confirmed.

transcript.text: I have a compliance requirement to add. I confirmed with the audit team this afternoon that evidence showing every internet-facing service patched is due by Friday 12:00 UTC, and an exception would not satisfy this review. I have not added this requirement to the security ticket yet because the audit team's written confirmation arrived only minutes ago. This means the broad deployment on Friday must be completed early enough that we can produce and submit patching evidence for all internet-facing services before Friday 12:00 UTC.
